children: Brent crude could climb to $120 a barrel if attacks on shipping in the Middle East intensify, Goldman Sachs's Daan Struyven says in an interview with Bloomberg. "The events over the last few days do suggest the risk of shipping disruptions broadening and intensifying is an important one," the co-head of global commodities ​research says. In a scenario where exports from the region normalize, Brent is seen at $80 a barrel, in line with the level of OECD commercial stocks, according to Struyven. The global oil benchmark currently trades around $97 a barrel. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
